doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: Bass in modern records and the importance of the bass player
summary: Why bass dominates today's records through speakers and technology, and why Gold hires the bass player first.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I sometimes think of music — when you're switching radio stations for instance — you're listening to something from '58, '64, into the hip hop era. And if music was a pie chart, if the audio — to me it used to be that the vocal had the biggest slice of the pie. Now I hear bass as like the predominant thing that people hear.

Well you know what? I think it's — the record business, if you're really into the record business, is really created about through the inventions of all the technology. And what happened back in those days you couldn't really get bass to really respond enormously on the radio speaker or on these little speakers that we had. And then as — when we went to the movie theater we got bass because they had those big Voice of Music speakers that were this big. When we went to the studio we got bass because those were the same speakers that were there too. But people didn't have them in their homes. Now they've got © Fillius Jazz Archive 6

little speakers this big you have so much bass coming out of it it's incredible. So I think, and then I think that one of the things about bass — be it synth bass or regular bass — it makes the record have a lot more volume and power. So I think that's partially a lot of the reason.
I've always felt the basses can be the most important thing happening because it acts like a drum, it guides the harmony, and it takes a certain mindset to be a good and appropriate bass player.

I agree. And I agree it's one of the most important things. You know when I still get a chance to produce a whole record, when I hire — to me the bass player is the most important person I'm hiring. Because he'll drive the record, especially if it's R&B or disco or any of the kind of things that I get hired to do at this point in my life.
